date.as_written: harinmṛgāṃkayāṃjhava (!) veda pramite vatsare bhādrapadameva ka caturddaśyāṃ śauriyasrānvitāyāṃ

notes: The author is Appayya Dīkṣita (written 'appadīkṣita'). His name is given as the stem 'Appa' with 'dīkṣita' as a title. The year chronogram 'harinmṛgāṃkayāṃjhava (!) veda pramite' is corrupt. Only mṛgāṅka (= 1) and veda (= 4) can be read with confidence. Their order does not match 1845 read right to left, which would need a 5-4-8-1 word sequence, so the catalogue's 'SAM 1845' cannot be confirmed from the quoted text. The year 1845 and its era are taken from the catalogue. VS is assumed (= 1788 CE), but ŚS 1845 (= 1923 CE) cannot be strictly ruled out. 'bhādrapadameva ka' is read as 'bhādrapade mecaka' (dark fortnight), which gives kṛṣṇa pakṣa. 'śauriyasrānvitāyāṃ' is read as 'śaurivāsarānvitāyāṃ' (Saturday, Sauri = Saturn). 'vipaśvit' = vipaścit, 'learned', is an epithet. The catalogue's scribe name 'Pipaśvī' comes from misreading this epithet as part of the name. The place phrase is corrupt: 'vyapāla' may stand for 'nepāla' (…rāṣṭrasya nepāla…), and 'vāhinīpariveṣṭite' means 'surrounded by rivers'. The place has not been identified.
